title: A Steeper Cornea

patient.name: Mr Hafiz Bin Rahman
patient.presenting_complaint: Referred for corneal topography — worsening, hard-to-correct astigmatism and frequent eye rubbing

history.hpc: Mr Hafiz says 'My glasses keep changing, and the optical shop say my astigmatism very high. I always rub my eyes also.' His refraction is unstable with high irregular astigmatism, and the doctor ordered topography to screen for keratoconus.
history.pmhx: Allergic eyes with frequent rubbing. No previous eye surgery.

examination_findings.anterior_segment: Clear corneas on slit lamp; high astigmatism
examination_findings.fundus: Not the focus of this station

corneal_topography.pattern: Inferior corneal steepening with an asymmetric bow-tie and irregular astigmatism
corneal_topography.interpretation: Pattern is suspicious for keratoconus; flagged for the doctor
corneal_topography.quality: Good capture quality on repeated scans

diagnosis: Corneal topography shows inferior steepening with an asymmetric bow-tie and irregular astigmatism — a pattern suspicious for keratoconus, fitting the picture of unstable high astigmatism and frequent eye rubbing. The OT obtains good-quality maps and flags the suspicious pattern for the doctor; the OT does not diagnose.

immediate: Confirm identity and that both eyes are to be mapped
Confirm any contact lens washout period before mapping
Explain the non-contact scan and position the patient on the corneal apex
Capture good-quality topography for both eyes, repeating poor captures
Recognise the inferior steepening / asymmetric bow-tie as a keratoconus-suspicious pattern
Provide the maps to the doctor and flag the suspicious pattern
Document the findings and capture quality
follow_up: Doctor to assess for keratoconus and consider monitoring / treatment
Advise the patient to avoid eye rubbing
patient_education: Explain the scan maps the shape of the cornea
Advise strongly against rubbing the eyes, which can worsen the cornea
Reassure that the doctor will review the maps

key_points: Confirms identity and that both eyes are mapped
Asks about eye rubbing and unstable astigmatism
Confirms contact lens washout if relevant
Aligns on the corneal apex and captures good-quality maps
Knows the keratoconus pattern (inferior steepening, asymmetric bow-tie)
Links eye rubbing and unstable astigmatism as risk features
Does not diagnose — flags for the doctor
Provides maps and flags the suspicious pattern to the doctor
Advises the patient against eye rubbing
